# Washington State SAAM Policy Reference

## SAAM Chapter Matrix

| SAAM Section | Source Pattern from `Complete_SAAM_26A-05_2026_07_01-1.pdf` | Implementation Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1.10.10 | SAAM policies are minimum standards and agencies add stricter detail when the baseline remains intact. | Model statewide-required fields first, then layer agency extensions without breaking the base contract. |
| 1.10.20 | OFM establishes a GAAP-based accounting system under RCW 43.88.160. | Trace validation rules and reporting contracts to GAAP-aligned statewide policy ownership. |
| 20.15.10 | Internal control supports operations, reporting, and compliance objectives with reasonable assurance. | Capture approver identity, timestamp, source document, exception reason, and segregation metadata on controlled events. |
| 75.10.10 | Chapter 75 separates mandatory statewide codes from agency-designated codes. | Keep mandatory AFRS-facing codes in governed reference data and isolate agency extensions beside them. |
| 75.30.10 | Chapter 75 publishes GAAP fund types and statewide fund type codes. | Store fund type, fund code, and statement mapping as explicit effective-dated attributes. |
| 85.15.05 | SAAM budgetary entries are generated by TALS and recorded in AFRS as illustrative statewide patterns. | Align appropriation, allotment, reserve, and close workflows with TALS-to-AFRS budgetary event shapes. |

## Statewide Accounting Reference

| Topic | Washington State Pattern | Agent Output |
|---|---|---|
| AFRS integration | Agency transactions flow through statewide accounting structures, mandatory codes, and validation rules. | Data contracts, validation tables, and export mappings aligned to AFRS-facing fields. |
| Fiscal year and periods | State fiscal year, accounting periods, and close states drive recognition and lapse behavior. | Period dimension with fiscal year, accounting month, close state, and effective dates. |
| Appropriation and allotment | SAAM Chapter 85 ties authority, allotment, reserve, and close events to budgetary accounting entries. | Appropriation ledger, allotment ledger, reserve events, and variance views. |
| Fund and statement coding | SAAM Chapter 75.30.10 maps GAAP fund types to statewide codes such as `AA`, `BA`, `CA`, and `FA`. | Effective-dated fund code tables with fund-type and statement-mapping attributes. |
| Vendor payment processing | Payment flows need approval, coding, and statewide process compatibility. | Payment request aggregates, approval evidence, and remittance support data. |
| Internal control | SAAM Chapter 20 frames control over operations, reporting, and compliance objectives. | Control checkpoints, exception logs, segregation checks, and evidence links. |

## SAAM Integration

| Integration Area | Agent Action | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| Policy mapping | Agent stores SAAM section references, effective dates, and rule ownership beside validation or workflow rules. | Every state-specific rule traces to a named policy area and effective period. |
| AFRS data contracts | Agent defines fields for appropriation, allotment, object code, subobject, revenue source, fund, vendor, and fiscal period context. | Export and import contracts carry the statewide coding set required by the use case. |
| Control evidence | Agent records approval chain, exception reason, correction path, and audit timestamp on controlled events. | Control evidence supports reconciliation and external review. |
| Period-close snapshots | Agent publishes immutable close snapshots for agency and statewide reporting support. | Operational adjustments after close do not rewrite published close artifacts. |
| Code-list governance | Agent centralizes object codes, revenue source codes, and related lookup tables with effective dating. | Validation services reject inactive or misdated codes. |
| Change management | Agent versions policy and code mappings when SAAM directives or corrections change the rule set. | Historical transactions retain the correct effective-date logic. |

## Public Sector Specific Patterns

| Pattern | Use | Implementation Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Effective-dated policy rules | State policy changes need historical fidelity | Store section reference, version, effective date, and retirement date on validation rules |
| Statewide baseline plus agency extension | Agency detail varies while statewide structure stays stable | Use extension tables or value objects that preserve the base statewide schema |
| Appropriation-aware posting | Authority and accounting move together | Require appropriation and allotment context on budget-controlled transactions |
| Code-list validation service | Standardized codes drive reliable statewide reporting | Expose object, revenue, and fund code validators with effective-date filtering |
| Payment control evidence | Vendor payment workflows need auditable approvals | Persist approval checkpoints, exception handling, and remittance linkage |

## Integration Hooks

| Surface | Agent Action | Output |
|---|---|---|
| EF Core | Model effective-dated code lists, appropriation ledgers, allotments, vendor payments, and control evidence with explicit foreign keys and period indexes. | State-compliant persistence layer |
| Microsoft Fabric | Publish statewide-coded facts and compliance dimensions for appropriation, allotment, object code, revenue source, and payment monitoring. | Agency and statewide reporting datasets |
| Integration services | Separate import, validation, correction, and export stages for AFRS-facing and payment-facing interfaces. | Traceable interface pipelines with exception handling |

## Common Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Agent Fix |
|---|---|
| SAAM references land in prose only | Agent stores policy references as structured metadata on rules and workflows. |
| AFRS-facing integrations flatten effective dates out of code lists | Agent applies effective-dated lookup tables and historical validation. |
| Agency extensions replace statewide base fields | Agent keeps statewide-required fields stable and layers extensions beside them. |
| Vendor payment approvals stay outside the system record | Agent persists approval checkpoints and exception evidence in the core workflow. |
| State fiscal period logic relies on calendar month only | Agent models fiscal year, accounting period, close state, and lapse behavior explicitly. |
